title: Will Bo Nix’s long‑awaited return reveal Broncos’ true offensive potential? | Orange & Blue Today
text: Bo Nix is finally set to take the field — his first game action since the ankle injury in last year’s Divisional Round — and the Broncos’ second preseason game against the Packers suddenly feels a whole lot bigger. So what should fans expect from the third‑year QB. A controlled script, quick rhythm throws, and a chance to show the command he’s displayed all camp. The snap count won’t be huge, but it should be meaningful — enough to knock off rust and give Denver its first real look at how the offense operates with Nix at the controls. And yes, Jaylen Waddle is expected to be out there too. When Nix and Waddle share the field, the spacing, tempo, and explosiveness instantly change. This could be our first glimpse of just how high‑powered this offense might be once the regular season arrives. Rookie RB Jonah Coleman will also be under the microscope after a fantastic debut. Can he stack performances. Can he push for a real role. Denver wants to see consistency, physicality, and continued confidence. It’s a preseason game — but it’s also a preview of what this offense could become. 🔥 In this episode: Bo Nix’s long‑awaited return and realistic expectations Projected snap count for the Broncos’ franchise QB Jaylen Waddle’s impact if he suits up Jonah Coleman’s next step after a breakout debut Whether we finally see the offense’s true ceiling Drop your Broncos take — what do YOU want to see from Nix’s debut, and which player has the best chance to steal the show against Green Bay.

title: BEARS-BENGALS JOINT PRACTICE: Thoughts, Observations, Standouts and More
channel_name: Hoge & Jahns: a show about the Chicago Bears
text: Hoge & Jahns are in Cincinnati after the Bears and Bengals wrapped up a joint practice ahead of Saturday’s preseason matchup. The guys break down what they saw from the Bears on both sides of the ball, including the offense’s red-zone success and the latest developments at left tackle. Plus, we hear from TJ Edwards on playing with Devin Bush, and the development of rookies Malik MuhammadDillon Thieneman. Plus, he addresses the absence of Kyler Gordon. Finally, we hear from Jay Morrison of BengalsTalk.com to get the Bengals’ perspective ahead of Saturday's game against the Bengals in Cinncinati. Hosted by Simplecast, an AdsWizz company. See https://pcm.adswizz.com for information about our collection and use of personal data for advertising.

title: [FULL EPISODE] Bears offense has a roller coaster day against Bengals in joint practice
channel_name: Take The North: A Chicago Bears Podcast
text: It was a bit of an up-and-down day for the Bears as they held a joint practice with the Bengals in Cincinnati. Dan Wiederer and Mark Grote bring in Athletic writer Kevin Fishbain, who was in Cincinnati to witness the practice in person. What was the good and what was the bad for quarterback Caleb Williams and the offense? Can we expect the Bears to play their starters when they face the Bengals in their preseason game Saturday?
